Daily Digest · Computer Science

Multimodal Learning Transforms Scientific Discovery and Medical Imaging

Today's submissions reveal a decisive shift toward integrated multimodal systems that combine visual, molecular, and textual data for scientific understanding. From spatial transcriptomics fused with histopathology to agentic medical control frameworks, researchers are moving beyond single-modality approaches. Notably, foundation models and lightweight linguistic classifiers are proving surprisingly effective across diverse domains—challenging assumptions about what requires scale.

Computer Vision
Multimodal Histology Meets Gene Expression at Scale

HistoTx pioneer early fusion of H&E pathology images with spatial transcriptomics at varying resolutions, enabling both morphology and molecular profiling as true input modalities rather than just training signals. This self-supervised approach opens genuine multi-input inference for tissue biology.

First model to treat transcriptomics as an equal input modality rather than auxiliary training signal, enabling molecule-aware image understanding.
Driessen, Malmsten et al. 2611.02681 PDF
Computer Vision
Sketches Now Ground Real-World Object Detection

Sketch-Omni extends promptable perception MLLMs to sketch-to-photo detection for the first time, allowing users to draw an object in a sketch and localize it in photographs. It also performs all standard tasks (detection, referring expressions, affordance grounding) directly on sketch inputs.

First perception MLLM to enable bidirectional sketch↔photo grounding, opening sketch-driven visual search in real images.
Wang, Chen et al. 2611.04262 PDF
AI Safety
LLM Unlearning Now Verifiable via Statistical Independence

PINT introduces the first unlearning algorithm that provably removes statistical dependence between forgotten tokens and model representations using the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion. Prior work left memorized content statistically detectable; this ensures true forgetting.

First unlearning method with formal statistical guarantees that forgotten data becomes independent from internal representations.
Shkabrii, Plant et al. 2611.03955 PDF
Machine Learning
Lightweight Linguistics Detect AI-Generated Peer Reviews

SAGE achieves 0.9566 AUROC using only speech act annotations and subjectivity features—no large classifiers needed. This shows human subjectivity patterns remain distinguishable in AI text, enabling practical detector deployments.

Linguistically-grounded classifier outperforms scale, reaching 95.66% AUROC with minimal features on real peer review detection.
Freijedo Aduna, Yaiche et al. 2611.03060 PDF

Featured Researcher
YZ
Yi-Zhe Song
Researcher · Sketch & Visual Understanding

Yi-Zhe Song leads work at the intersection of sketch, vision, and visual understanding, pioneering human-sketch-machine interaction. His lab has established sketch as a powerful modality for retrieval, synthesis, and now perception grounding. Today's Sketch-Omni contribution demonstrates the maturation of sketch-based visual prompting into practical perception tasks.
